why: T40 (D39). so3_average is advertised as an SO(3)-averaged regulariser. If the velocity field is equivariant, rotating x_t and the target by the same R leaves the MSE unchanged, so averaging over K rotations averages K copies of one number — the term becomes a scaled duplicate of the FM MSE and contributes no gradient direction of its own.
decision: KEEP the code path; do not delete. Deleting it would change what the archived configs mean, and the kill clause in T40 requires a 288-step run to show the 0.1 weight changes the FM trajectory by more than 2% — which cannot be run under the current no-training directive. Instead the duplication is stated at launch.

c8_per_epoch.note: the only run on disk with so3_average: true
c8_per_epoch.verdict: COPY — the ratio equals so3_average_weight (0.1) to 9 significant figures at every epoch

measurements.mechanism: For an equivariant field v(Rx) = R v(x), the K-term average of MSE(v(R_k x_t), R_k dx) equals MSE(v(x_t), dx) for every k, so the average is the identity. The residual 2e-9 is float32 rounding in the rotation matmuls, not a broken equivariance layer.
measurements.effective_fm_coefficient: fm_weight * (1 + so3_average_weight) = 1.0 * 1.1 on c8, i.e. the run trained with an FM coefficient 10% above the configured 1.0

red_check.equivariant_field: the average is a no-op (ratio == weight) — PASS
red_check.non_equivariant_field: the average is NOT a no-op (ratio != weight) — PASS, so the test can distinguish the two
red_check.trainer_banner: the launch states the effective FM coefficient when so3_average is on — PASS

honest_limits: The 0.1 weight is not proven irrelevant to the optimisation path. It multiplies the FM gradient by 1.1, which is a real 10% step-size change; the T40 kill clause (288 steps, fm_term trajectory within 2%) has not been run.
Only one run on disk ever enabled so3_average, so the constancy is measured over 3 epochs of one seed, not across seeds.
New configs should leave so3_average off and put the intended coefficient into fm_weight directly; the trainer now says so at launch.
